t.4.10.1: Then, wishing to please him, I sought to placate my brother, who had come to me filled with wrath and greatly agitated.
t.4.10.2: By good fortune you have returned safe and well, and the enemy has been slain by you. For you alone are the protector of me, who am without a protector, you who bring joy to the helpless.
t.4.10.3: This many-ribbed umbrella of yours, like the full moon newly risen, together with the yak-tail fan, which I hold up for you, accept it.
t.4.10.4: You alone are the king, worthy of honour, and I am ever as I was before. This kingdom, which was held only as a trust, I now return to you.
t.4.10.5: Do not be angry with me, gentle one, O destroyer of enemies; I beseech you, O king, bowing my head, and I have joined my palms in supplication.
t.4.10.6: The ministers and the citizens, coming together, forcibly installed me in the kingship, out of their desire to secure the leaderless land.
t.4.10.8: Having assembled the subjects and also the esteemed ministers, he spoke to me, in the midst of our friends, words that were utterly reproachful.
t.4.10.7: Though I spoke to him so affectionately, that monkey rebuked me, and after saying to me, "Shame on you!", he went on to say a great many such things.
t.4.10.9: It is known to you how, in the night, that great asura Māyāvī, cruel, eager for battle and exceedingly wicked-minded, challenged me.
t.4.10.10: Hearing that roar of his, I came out of the royal palace, and this exceedingly fierce brother of mine swiftly followed after me.
t.4.10.11: But that mighty one, the moment he saw me in the night together with a companion, fled, stricken with fear; seeing him, the two of us pursued him. Pursued swiftly, he entered a great cave.
t.4.10.13: Without slaying him, I have no power to return from here to the city. Wait at the mouth of the cave until I kill him.
t.4.10.12: Knowing that he had entered that very dreadful and very vast cave, I then addressed this brother of mine, who is cruel of aspect.
t.4.10.14: Thinking, “He is lurking here,” I entered that impenetrable cave; and while I was searching for him, a year then passed.
t.4.10.15: But through unflagging perseverance I found that fearsome enemy, and there I slew that asura together with his kinsmen.
t.4.10.16: As he lay roaring on the ground, the torrent of blood that gushed from his mouth filled that cave and made it impassable.
t.4.10.17: Having slain that valiant enemy, the son of Dundubhi, I saw, even as I was coming out, that the mouth of the cave had been blocked.
t.4.10.18: But when, as I cried out again and again, "Sugrīva! Sugrīva!", there was no reply, then I became deeply distressed.
t.4.10.19: But with many blows of my feet I broke it open; then, coming out through that opening, I have returned again, as you see.
t.4.10.20: There I was shut in by him, the cruel Sugrīva, who, seeking the kingdom for himself, had forgotten the affection due to a brother.
t.4.10.21: Having spoken thus to me there, the monkey Vālī, free of all fear, then banished me with but a single garment.
t.4.10.22: By him I was cast out and robbed of my wife, O Rāghava; and out of fear of him I have roamed this entire earth with its forests and oceans.
t.4.10.23: Grieving over the abduction of my wife, I entered Ṛśyamūka, the best of mountains, which for a particular reason is unassailable by Vālin.
t.4.10.24: All this, the long account of our enmity, has now been told to you. See, O Rāghava, the misfortune that has befallen me, though I am without fault.
t.4.10.26: Thus addressed, that radiant one, knower of dharma, began to speak to Sugrīva words in accord with dharma, as if smiling.
t.4.10.25: O hero, you who strike fear into all the worlds, you should show favour to me, who am tormented by fear of Vālin, by subduing him.
t.4.10.27: These sharpened arrows of mine, unfailing and blazing like the sun, will fall in fury upon that wicked Vālin.
t.4.10.28: Only so long as I do not see him, the one who carried off your wife, may that evil-souled Vālī, the defiler of right conduct, remain alive.
t.4.10.29: Inferring from my own experience, I see you sunk in an ocean of grief. I shall carry you across it; you will attain your desire in full.
